title: Vehicle energy use: road load and regeneration
summary: Where a car's energy goes on city and highway driving, and why regenerative braking reverses the city/highway order for electric cars.

concepts.label: Vehicle
concepts.description: A car, SUV, van or pickup variant tested by the EPA.

facts.text: fueleconomy.gov publishes the EPA test results for every US model since 1984.

children.label: Powertrain
children.description: Petrol, diesel, hybrid or battery electric.

children.label: Body type
children.description: Car, SUV, van or pickup: a proxy for frontal area and drag coefficient.

children.label: Drag area CdA
children.description: Drag coefficient times frontal area, m²: what sets the drag at a given speed. Not in the EPA data.

concepts.label: Energy per distance
concepts.description: kWh per 100 km on a test cycle.

children.label: Highway/city ratio
children.description: Highway energy over city energy per km: below 1 the highway is cheaper.

children.label: Highway penalty
children.description: Highway minus city energy per 100 km, mostly drag for an EV.

concepts.label: Road load
concepts.description: The force needed to drive: F = A + B v + C v² (rolling resistance, drivetrain, air drag).

facts.text: EPA test cars carry road-load coefficients A, B, C from coast-down tests.

children.label: Aerodynamic drag
children.description: ½ ρ Cd A v²: per km it grows with v².

children.label: Braking losses
children.description: ½ m v² per stop: lost in friction brakes, mostly recovered by regenerative braking.

children.label: Rolling resistance
children.description: Tyre losses, roughly constant per km (Crr · m · g).

concepts.label: Test cycle
concepts.description: EPA's UDDS (city) and HWFET (highway) speed traces.

facts.text: UDDS: 12.07 km in 1369 s; HWFET: 16.45 km in 765 s.

concepts.label: Temperature
concepts.description: Cold air raises drag and rolling resistance a little and EV heating loads a lot; not in this data.
